title: Real-time neural processing pipeline
text:
Overview
The ReHAB trial depends on a low-latency neural processing pipeline. I rebuilt that C++ path so it could keep up with live human recordings without the previous memory and runtime cost.

title: Real-time neural processing pipeline
text:
What I did

Redesigned the pipeline with lock-free multithreading.
Reduced the footprint by 88% and improved performance by 46%.
Added internal latency profiling and benchmark instruments to automate debugging and telemetry across days.
Trained PyTorch models for regression and classification of neural dynamics and disease states on top of the faster path.

title: Real-time neural processing pipeline
text:
Tools
C++, PyTorch, Docker, custom latency and telemetry tooling

title: Closed-Loop Agentic Module (CLAM)
text:
Overview
CLAM is the closed-loop agentic module I lead on the ReHAB (Reconnecting Hand-Arm-Brain) clinical trial. The goal is to let field-deployed agents operate a real-time bioelectric pipeline while staying inside clinical safety constraints.

title: Closed-Loop Agentic Module (CLAM)
text:
What I did

Built LangGraph harnesses so agents can rebalance across the cloud, review their own code, and run design, implementation, and review in parallel.
Closed the loop with medical-grade neurostimulators so output waveforms feed back into the agent environment for continuous improvement, safety checks, and debugging.
Isolated autonomous agents from sensitive data with Docker containerization and local LLMs.
Added latency profiling and multi-day telemetry so the team can debug the system under trial conditions.

title: Closed-Loop Agentic Module (CLAM)
text:
Tools
LangGraph, Python, Docker, local LLMs, C#, medical-grade neurostimulators

title: Samuel Boyer
text:
About me
Welcome. I am a part-time graduate student at Case Western Reserve University and a software engineer on the ReHAB (Reconnecting Hand-Arm-Brain) clinical trial.
I work as a forward deployed engineer in neural engineering and brain–computer interfaces, with a focus on real-time, low-latency bioelectric pipelines and field-deployed AI workflows. In addition to coursework, I lead development of the Closed-Loop Agentic Module (CLAM) used in live human studies.
If you would like to reach me, write to sam.james.boyer@gmail.com or use the GitHub link above.
